circuitous

/ser-KYOO-ih-tuhs/ - the stress falls on KYOO · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Circuitous means taking a long, indirect route rather than the direct one.

The ants took a circuitous trail around the whole counter, tripling the distance to the sugar bowl for no reason we could see.

Example

To get one lost library card reissued, Naomi collected a form from the registrar, a stamp from the bursar across campus, and a signature from an office open only every other Thursday. The process was circuitous by design, she suspected - a paper journey that visited every building except the library.

Circuitous fits because the route - here a procedural one - runs far out of its way to reach a simple destination. Winding wouldn't say that: a winding path can still be the shortest one. Circuitous always means the long way around, whether on roads, in paperwork, or in an apology.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

roundabout: Roundabout is the everyday word for not going straight at a thing - a roundabout route, a roundabout apology. Circuitous means the same in more formal dress and suits official contexts: audits, itineraries, legal processes. If you would say it to a friend, use roundabout; in a report, circuitous.

meandering: Meandering means drifting lazily and aimlessly, curve by curve, like a slow river with nowhere to be. A circuitous route can be brisk and purposeful - it simply runs far out of its way. Meandering is about lacking an aim; circuitous is about the distance, not the mood.

tortuous: Tortuous means full of twists and turns - it measures how tangled a path is, bend by bend. Circuitous measures something else: how far the way strays from direct. A mountain switchback is tortuous yet efficient; a detour looping around two counties is circuitous without one sharp turn.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

direct: straight to the destination or the point

straight: the shortest line between two places

Where it sits · how far the route strays from direct — winding → circuitous → labyrinthine

winding vs. circuitous: A winding lane curves prettily and may still be the shortest way home; circuitous goes further, insisting the way runs far out of its way.

labyrinthine vs. circuitous: Labyrinthine outdoes circuitous: a circuitous route is long but gets you there by one traceable path, while a labyrinthine one tangles into so many turns you may be lost for good.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — circuit

Root — circuit: a going around; a circle

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: characterized by

Put it together

Put it together: Circuit (a going around) + -ous (characterized by) = characterized by going around. Latin circuitus came from circum (around) + ire (to go): a circuitous route, explanation, or refund process quite simply 'goes around' rather than straight to the point.

Use the root in a new word: circumference

Use the root in a new word: circumference: The park sign lists the giant sequoia's circumference just under its age and height.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal

Circuitous describes routes and processes - real roads or paper-trail errands - that run the long way around. It says nothing about hiding: a circuitous explanation eventually arrives at its point, where a cryptic one (this unit) hides the point on purpose. For everyday talk, roundabout does the same job in plainer clothes.
